docs.title: mailforen Documentation
docs.text: Advanced OSINT toolkit for email forensics and digital investigations.

docs.title: ⚠️ For Authorized Use Only
docs.text: This tool is intended for legitimate security investigations, phishing incident response, and defensive OSINT. Users must have explicit permission to investigate targets. Use for unauthorized reconnaissance, harassment, or malicious purposes is strictly prohibited and may be illegal.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Email Forensics — Parse .eml headers, analyze authentication (SPF/DMARC/MX), trace Received chains
  • Domain & IP Intelligence — DNS lookups, ASN/org lookup via public APIs, Certificate Transparency search
  • URL Tracing — Safe redirect chain analysis with loop detection
  • Username Pivoting — Correlate identities across public platforms
  • File Metadata — Extract EXIF data from images/documents
  • Case Management — SQLite-backed investigation case tracking
  • Evidence Export — Reports in Markdown, HTML, PDF, and JSON/SIEM formats
  • Passive-First Design — All checks passive by default; active checks require --unsafe opt-in

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ritchegerona/mailforen.git
cd mailforen
pip install -e .

For development: 

pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: First Investigation
docs.text:
# 1. Create a case
mailforen case new "Phishing-001" --target suspicious.example.com

# 2. Analyze email
mailforen email headers suspicious.eml --case-id 1
mailforen email auth suspicious.example.com --case-id 1

# 3. Investigate infrastructure
mailforen domain intel suspicious.example.com --case-id 1
mailforen ip intel 203.0.113.42 --case-id 1

# 4. Generate report
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format html

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Python API reference for mailforen modules. All modules expose a singleton instance at module level.

docs.title: mailforen.core.config.Settings
docs.text:
Pydantic Settings configuration. All fields overrideable via MAILFOREN_ environment variables or .env file.

from mailforen.core.config import settings

settings.data_dir        # Path: ~/.mailforen (created on import)
settings.debug           # bool: False
settings.user_agent      # str: "mailforen/0.1.0 (OSINT Research Tool)"
settings.timeout         # int: 30 (seconds)
settings.max_retries     # int: 3 (not currently used)
settings.rate_limit_delay # float: 1.0 (seconds between requests)
settings.proxy           # str | None
settings.allow_unsafe    # bool: False (set by --unsafe flag)
settings.virustotal_api_key   # str | None
settings.shodan_api_key       # str | None
settings.securitytrails_api_key # str | None
settings.emailrep_api_key     # str | None

docs.title: mailforen.core.db.CaseDB
docs.text:
SQLite-backed case and evidence management. Singleton: db = CaseDB().

from mailforen.core.db import db

# Create a new case
case_id = db.create_case(name: str, target: str | None = None, description: str | None = None) -> int

# List all cases
cases = db.list_cases() -> list[dict]

# Get case by ID
case = db.get_case(case_id: int) -> dict | None

# Add a finding to a case
finding_id = db.add_finding(
    case_id: int,
    module: str,           # e.g. "email.headers", "email.auth"
    input_data: str,       # original input (file path, domain, IP, etc.)
    result: dict,          # module output
    risk_level: str = "info",  # "info" | "low" | "medium" | "high"
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    notes: str | None = None
) -> int

# Get all findings for a case
findings = db.get_findings(case_id: int) -> list[dict]

Database Schema: - cases(id, name UNIQUE, target, description, created_at, updated_at, status) - findings(id, case_id, module, input_data, result_json, risk_level, tags, notes, timestamp) - requests(id, case_id, url, method, module, timestamp, response_code) — schema only, not used

Note: Foreign keys declared but not enforced (no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON). No update/delete methods.

docs.title: mailforen.core.http.HTTPClient
docs.text:
HTTP client with rate limiting and safety features. Singleton: http_client = HTTPClient().

from mailforen.core.http import http_client

# GET request (follows redirects)
response = http_client.get(url: str, params: dict | None = None, **kwargs) -> httpx.Response | None

# HEAD request (does NOT follow redirects - for URL tracing)
response = http_client.head(url: str, **kwargs) -> httpx.Response | None

Behavior: - New httpx.Client created per request - Returns None on any exception (logged at ERROR) - Rate limited by settings.rate_limit_delay (default 1.0s) - Uses settings.proxy if configured - HEAD explicitly uses follow_redirects=False to allow manual redirect tracing

docs.title: mailforen.core.logger
docs.text:
from mailforen.core.logger import logger, setup_logger

logger = setup_logger(name: str = "mailforen") -> logging.Logger

Configuration: - Log file: ~/.mailforen/logs/mailforen.log (DEBUG level) - Console: RichHandler at INFO level - File format: %(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s

docs.title: mailforen.core.safety
docs.text:
Safety gate for active checks.

from mailforen.core.safety import require_unsafe, UnsafeModeRequired

require_unsafe(action: str) -> None
    # Raises UnsafeModeRequired if settings.allow_unsafe is False
    # Logs WARNING when allowed

docs.title: mailforen.modules.email.headers.HeaderAnalyzer
docs.text:
Parse .eml files and extract headers. Singleton: header_analyzer = HeaderAnalyzer().

from mailforen.modules.email.headers import header_analyzer

result = header_analyzer.analyze_file(file_path: Path) -> dict
result = header_analyzer.analyze_message(msg) -> dict  # email.message.Message

Return dict keys: - from, to, subject, date, message_id, reply_to, return_path - received_chain: list of {"hop": int, "raw": str} (newest first, hop 1 = topmost) - authentication_results: raw Authentication-Results header - received_spf: raw Received-SPF header - user_agent: always None (not populated) - x_mailer: X-Mailer header value - originating_ips: list of IPv4 addresses from Received headers (deduped, loopback excluded)

Errors: Returns {"error": str} on parse failure.

docs.title: mailforen.modules.email.auth.EmailAuthChecker
docs.text:
Check SPF, DMARC, MX via DNS. Singleton: auth_checker = EmailAuthChecker().

from mailforen.modules.email.auth import auth_checker

result = auth_checker.check_all(domain: str) -> dict
result = auth_checker.check_spf(domain: str) -> dict
result = auth_checker.check_dmarc(domain: str) -> dict
result = auth_checker.check_mx(domain: str) -> dict

Return structures:

check_spf / check_dmarc: 

{"found": bool, "records": list[str]}  # on success
{"found": False, "error": str}         # on DNS failure

check_mx: 

{"found": bool, "records": [{"priority": int, "exchange": str}]}  # sorted by priority

check_all: 

{
    "domain": str,
    "spf": {...},
    "dmarc": {...},
    "mx": {...}
}

Note: DKIM verification is not implemented despite being advertised in docstrings/README.

docs.title: mailforen.modules.forensic.domain.DomainIntel
docs.text:
DNS record gathering. Singleton: domain_intel = DomainIntel().

from mailforen.modules.forensic.domain import domain_intel

result = domain_intel.get_all_records(domain: str) -> dict
result = domain_intel.get_a_records(domain: str) -> list[str]
result = domain_intel.get_aaaa_records(domain: str) -> list[str]
result = domain_intel.get_mx_records(domain: str) -> list[dict]
result = domain_intel.get_ns_records(domain: str) -> list[str]
result = domain_intel.get_txt_records(domain: str) -> list[str]
result = domain_intel.get_cname_records(domain: str) -> list[str]

Returns empty list on DNS failure (logged at DEBUG).

Note: WHOIS/RDAP lookups not implemented.

docs.title: mailforen.modules.forensic.ip.IPIntel
docs.text:
IP intelligence via reverse DNS and ipinfo.io. Singleton: ip_intel = IPIntel().

from mailforen.modules.forensic.ip import ip_intel

result = ip_intel.get_info(ip: str) -> dict
result = ip_intel.reverse_dns(ip: str) -> str | None
result = ip_intel.get_asn_info(ip: str) -> dict

get_info returns: 

{
    "ip": str,
    "reverse_dns": str | None,
    "ptr": str | None  # duplicate of reverse_dns
}

get_asn_info queries https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json (no API key). Returns {} on failure.

docs.title: mailforen.modules.forensic.ct.CTSearch
docs.text:
Certificate Transparency search via crt.sh. Singleton: ct_search = CTSearch().

from mailforen.modules.forensic.ct import ct_search

result = ct_search.search(domain: str) -> dict

Returns: 

{
    "domain": str,
    "certificates_found": int,
    "unique_subdomains": list[str],  # sorted, wildcard-free, suffix-matched
    "raw_count": int
}

On error: {"domain": str, "error": str}

Algorithm: Queries https://crt.sh/?q=%.{domain}&output=json, splits name_value on newlines, keeps names where name.endswith(domain) and no wildcard.

docs.title: mailforen.modules.forensic.urltrace.URLTracer
docs.text:
Safe redirect chain tracing. Singleton: url_tracer = URLTracer().

from mailforen.modules.forensic.urltrace import url_tracer

result = url_tracer.trace(url: str) -> dict

Returns: 

{
    "original_url": str,
    "redirect_chain": [
        {"step": int, "url": str, "status_code": int}
    ],
    "final_url": str,
    "total_redirects": int
}

Behavior: - Max 10 hops - Uses HEAD first, falls back to GET if no response - Follows 301, 302, 303, 307, 308 only - Resolves relative Location headers - Tracks visited URLs to prevent loops

docs.title: mailforen.modules.forensic.filemeta.FileMetaExtractor
docs.text:
File metadata and EXIF extraction. Singleton: file_meta = FileMetaExtractor().

from mailforen.modules.forensic.filemeta import file_meta

result = file_meta.extract(file_path: Path) -> dict

Returns: 

{
    "filename": str,
    "path": str,          # absolute
    "size_bytes": int,
    "size_human": str,    # e.g. "1.5 MB"
    "created": str,       # ISO format from st_ctime
    "modified": str,      # ISO format from st_mtime
    "accessed": str,      # ISO format from st_atime
    "extension": str,     # lowercase suffix
    "exif": dict | None   # only for .jpg/.jpeg/.tiff/.tif
}

On missing file: {"error": "File not found"}

Note: No hashing (MD5/SHA256), no MIME detection despite python-magic dependency.

docs.title: mailforen.reports.generator.ReportGenerator
docs.text:
Multi-format report generation. Singleton: report_generator = ReportGenerator().

from mailforen.reports.generator import report_generator

path = report_generator.generate(case_id: int, format: str = "html") -> Path

Formats: "json", "markdown" / "md", "html", "pdf"

PDF generation: Tries weasyprint first, falls back to pdfkit (wkhtmltopdf). On total failure, returns the HTML path instead of raising.

Output directory: ~/.mailforen/reports/

Filename pattern: report_{case_name}_{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}.{ext}

Report data structure: 

{
    "case": {...},
    "findings": [...],
    "generated_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "tool": "mailforen v0.1.0"
}

docs.title: mailforen.utils.validators.Validators
docs.text:
Input validation helpers. Singleton: validators = Validators().

from mailforen.utils.validators import validators

validators.is_email(email: str) -> bool
validators.is_domain(domain: str) -> bool
validators.is_ip(ip: str) -> bool
validators.is_url(url: str) -> bool
validators.extract_domain_from_email(email: str) -> str | None

Note: Validators are defined but not currently used by the CLI for input validation.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: High-level architecture of mailforen.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text: Principle Implementation Passive-First All checks are passive by default; --unsafe opt-in required for any target contact Hermetic Testing Zero network access in tests; DNS/HTTP stubbed; temp data dir per session Case-Centric Every finding tied to a SQLite case for evidence tracking Singleton Services Config, DB, HTTP, Logger are module-level singletons No External Deps Required Works with only Python stdlib + PyPI deps (no system services)

docs.title: 1. Case Creation
docs.text:
mailforen case new "Name" --target X --desc Y
       │
       ▼
CaseDB.create_case() → INSERT INTO cases → returns case_id

docs.title: 2. Analysis Command (e.g., email auth example.com)
docs.text:
mailforen email auth example.com --case-id 1
       │
       ▼
EmailAuthChecker.check_all("example.com")
       │
       ├─── DNS TXT query for SPF
       ├─── DNS TXT query for _dmarc.example.com
       └─── DNS MX query for example.com
       │
       ▼
Result dict + risk_level ("medium" if SPF/DMARC missing else "low")
       │
       ▼
CaseDB.add_finding(case_id=1, module="email.auth", input_data="example.com", result=..., risk_level=...)
       │
       ▼
Rich console output + "✓ Added to case 1"

docs.title: 3. Report Generation
docs.text:
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format html
       │
       ▼
ReportGenerator.generate(1, "html")
       │
       ├─── CaseDB.get_case(1)
       ├─── CaseDB.get_findings(1)
       │
       ▼
Template rendering (Jinja2 for HTML, f-strings for MD, json.dump for JSON)
       │
       ▼
Write to ~/.mailforen/reports/report_{name}_{timestamp}.html
       │
       ▼
Return Path → console output

docs.title: Module Responsibilities
docs.text: Module Responsibility External Calls core/config Settings, env, data dirs Filesystem (mkdir) core/db SQLite CRUD for cases/findings SQLite (~/.mailforen/cases.db) core/http Rate-limited HTTP client Any HTTP(S) endpoint core/logger Structured logging Filesystem (~/.mailforen/logs/) core/safety Active-check gate — email/headers .eml parsing, header extraction — (stdlib email.parser) email/auth SPF/DMARC/MX via DNS System DNS resolver forensic/domain DNS record enumeration System DNS resolver forensic/ip Reverse DNS + ipinfo.io https://ipinfo.io forensic/ct CT log search https://crt.sh forensic/urltrace Redirect chain tracing Target URLs (HEAD/GET) forensic/filemeta File stats + EXIF — (stdlib, exifread) reports/generator Multi-format reports weasyprint / wkhtmltopdf (optional)

docs.title: Concurrency Model
docs.text:
• Single-threaded CLI — Typer commands run sequentially
  • GUI — PySide6 with QThread workers for background DNS/HTTP
  • HTTPClient — Not thread-safe; new httpx.Client per call
  • CaseDB — New SQLite connection per method; no connection pooling

docs.title: Security Boundaries
docs.text: Boundary Protection Target contact --unsafe flag + require_unsafe() gate (not yet enforced per-module) Rate limiting settings.rate_limit_delay (1s default) per HTTPClient instance Timeouts settings.timeout (30s default) on all HTTP Proxy settings.proxy respected by HTTPClient Input validation Validators exist but not used by CLI Path traversal Path objects, but no explicit sanitization SQL injection Parameterized queries (f-strings only for table names)

docs.title: Extension Points
docs.text:
1. New forensic module — Add to modules/forensic/, expose singleton, wire into CLI
  2. New report format — Add method to ReportGenerator, handle in generate()
  3. New authentication check — Add to EmailAuthChecker, update check_all() and CLI
  4. New pivot platform — Add to user_pivot_cmd platforms list
  5. API key integration — Use settings.*_api_key in new modules

docs.title: Known Architectural Debt
docs.text:
1. No dependency injection — Singletons make testing harder (mitigated by temp data dir in conftest)
  2. Foreign keys not enforced — PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF by default
  3. requests table unused — Schema exists but no request logging
  4. Validators unused — Defined but CLI doesn't validate inputs
  5. No retry logic — max_retries setting declared but not implemented
  6. GUI risk scoring diverges — EmailTab._auth_risk uses different rules than CLI
  7. Version single-sourced but not everywhere — __version__ in __init__.py, but config.py uses f-string at import time

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Complete command reference for the mailforen CLI toolkit.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: Option Description --unsafe Enable active checks that may contact targets directly (requires explicit confirmation) --help Show help message and exit

docs.title: Command Tree
docs.text: mailforen [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
• case - Case management
  • email - Email forensics and analysis
  • domain - Domain intelligence
  • ip - IP intelligence
  • ct - Certificate Transparency
  • url - URL analysis and tracing
  • user - Username/identity pivoting
  • file - File metadata analysis
  • report - Report generation

docs.title: mailforen version
docs.text:
Show version information.

mailforen version

Output: Rich panel displaying version and disclaimer notice.

docs.title: mailforen disclaimer
docs.text:
Show the project disclaimer.

mailforen disclaimer

Output: Contents of DISCLAIMER.md.

docs.title: case new
docs.text:
Create a new investigation case.

mailforen case new NAME [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - NAME (required) — Case name (must be unique)

Options: - -t, --target TEXT — Target domain, email, or IP - -d, --desc TEXT — Case description

Example: 

mailforen case new "Phishing-2024-001" --target suspicious.example.com --desc "Phishing campaign targeting finance dept"

docs.title: case list
docs.text:
List all cases.

mailforen case list

Output: Rich table with columns: ID, Name, Target, Status, Created.

docs.title: case show
docs.text:
Show details for a specific case.

mailforen case show CASE_ID

Arguments: - CASE_ID (required) — Numeric case ID

Output: Case details with findings table (risk levels color-coded: high=red, medium=yellow, low=green, info=cyan).

docs.title: email headers
docs.text:
Parse and analyze .eml file headers.

mailforen email headers FILE [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - FILE (required) — Path to .eml file

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: - From, To, Subject, Date, Message-ID, Reply-To, Return-Path - Received chain (hop-by-hop, newest first) - Authentication-Results header - Received-SPF header - X-Mailer - Originating IPs (extracted from Received headers, loopback excluded)

Example: 

mailforen email headers suspicious.eml --case-id 1

docs.title: email auth
docs.text:
Check email authentication (SPF, DMARC, MX) for a domain.

mailforen email auth DOMAIN [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - DOMAIN (required) — Domain to check

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: SPF records, DMARC policy, MX records with priorities.

Risk Assessment: - medium — SPF or DMARC missing - low — Both SPF and DMARC present

Example: 

mailforen email auth example.com --case-id 1

docs.title: domain intel
docs.text:
Gather DNS records for a domain.

mailforen domain intel DOMAIN [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - DOMAIN (required) — Domain to query

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME records.

Example: 

mailforen domain intel example.com --case-id 1

docs.title: ip intel
docs.text:
Gather intelligence for an IP address.

mailforen ip intel IP [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - IP (required) — IP address (IPv4 or IPv6)

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: - Reverse DNS (PTR) - ASN info via ipinfo.io (org, ASN, country, etc.) - Geolocation data

Example: 

mailforen ip intel 1.1.1.1 --case-id 1

docs.title: ct search
docs.text:
Search Certificate Transparency logs via crt.sh.

mailforen ct search DOMAIN [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - DOMAIN (required) — Domain to search for

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: Unique subdomains found in certificates (limited to 50 displayed, with count of additional).

Example: 

mailforen ct search example.com --case-id 1

docs.title: url trace
docs.text:
Trace URL redirect chain safely.

mailforen url trace URL [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - URL (required) — URL to trace

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: Redirect chain with step, status code, and URL. Max 10 hops.

Example: 

mailforen url trace https://bit.ly/example --case-id 1

docs.title: user pivot
docs.text:
Generate potential profile URLs for a username across platforms.

mailforen user pivot USERNAME [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - USERNAME (required) — Username to pivot on

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Platforms checked: GitHub, Twitter/X, Instagram, Reddit

Note: This performs passive URL construction only — no network requests are made.

Example: 

mailforen user pivot johndoe --case-id 1

docs.title: file meta
docs.text:
Extract file metadata and EXIF data.

mailforen file meta FILE [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - FILE (required) — Path to file

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER — Associate findings with a case

Output: - Filename, size (human-readable), timestamps (created, modified, accessed) - EXIF data (for JPEG/TIFF files only)

Example: 

mailforen file meta evidence.jpg --case-id 1

docs.title: report generate
docs.text:
Generate an investigation report.

mailforen report generate [OPTIONS]

Options: - -c, --case-id INTEGER (required) — Case ID to generate report for - -f, --format [html|markdown|md|pdf|json] — Output format (default: html)

Output: Report file saved to ~/.mailforen/reports/

Example: 

mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format html
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format pdf
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format json

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error (invalid input, missing file, case not found, etc.)

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All settings can be configured via environment variables with the MAILFOREN_ prefix:

Variable Default Description MAILFOREN_DATA_DIR ~/.mailforen Data directory (cases.db, logs, reports) MAILFOREN_DEBUG false Enable debug logging MAILFOREN_TIMEOUT 30 HTTP timeout in seconds MAILFOREN_RATE_LIMIT_DELAY 1.0 Minimum delay between requests (seconds) MAILFOREN_PROXY — HTTP proxy URL MAILFOREN_ALLOW_UNSAFE false Enable unsafe mode (same as --unsafe) MAILFOREN_VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY — VirusTotal API key MAILFOREN_SHODAN_API_KEY — Shodan API key MAILFOREN_SECURITYTRAILS_API_KEY — SecurityTrails API key MAILFOREN_EMAILREP_API_KEY — EmailRep API key

Can also be set in a .env file in the current working directory.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: Practical workflows and examples for mailforen.

docs.title: 1. Create a Case
docs.text:
mailforen case new "Invoice-Phishing-2024-03-15" \
  --target "payroll-services.example.com" \
  --desc "Phishing email targeting HR department with fake invoice attachment"

Output: 

✓ Created case Invoice-Phishing-2024-03-15 (ID: 1)

docs.title: 2. Analyze the Suspicious Email
docs.text:
# Parse headers
mailforen email headers invoice_phish.eml --case-id 1

# Check sender domain authentication
mailforen email auth payroll-services.example.com --case-id 1

docs.title: 3. Investigate Infrastructure
docs.text:
# Domain intelligence
mailforen domain intel payroll-services.example.com --case-id 1

# IP intelligence (from headers or domain A record)
mailforen ip intel 203.0.113.42 --case-id 1

# Certificate transparency
mailforen ct search payroll-services.example.com --case-id 1

# Trace any URLs in the email
mailforen url trace "https://bit.ly/fake-invoice-pdf" --case-id 1

docs.title: 4. Pivot on Identities
docs.text:
# If email mentions a username/handle
mailforen user pivot "john.doe.hr" --case-id 1

# Extract metadata from attachments
mailforen file meta invoice.pdf --case-id 1

docs.title: 5. Generate Report
docs.text:
# HTML (default) - best for viewing
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format html

# PDF - for evidence submission
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format pdf

# JSON - for SIEM ingestion
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format json

# Markdown - for documentation
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format markdown

Reports saved to ~/.mailforen/reports/.

docs.title: 6. Review Case
docs.text: mailforen case show 1

docs.title: Phishing Email Triage Checklist
docs.text: Step Command What to Look For 1. Headers email headers Mismatched From/Return-Path, suspicious Received hops, odd X-Mailer 2. Auth email auth SPF fail/softfail, no DMARC, DMARC p=none 3. Domain domain intel Newly registered, suspicious subdomains, unrelated MX 4. IPs ip intel Hosting providers, VPN/proxy ASNs, geo mismatch 5. CT ct search Many certs for lookalike domains 6. URLs url trace Long redirect chains, URL shorteners, credential harvesters 7. Attachments file meta Executables, macros, mismatched MIME

docs.title: Unsafe Mode (Active Checks)
docs.text:
Currently no active checks implemented. Reserved for future use:

mailforen --unsafe email auth example.com
# ⚠ Unsafe mode enabled: active checks may contact targets directly.

MAILFOREN_RATE_LIMIT_DELAY=2.0
MAILFOREN_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8080

docs.title: Python API Usage
docs.text:
from mailforen.core.config import settings
from mailforen.core.db import db
from mailforen.modules.email.auth import auth_checker
from mailforen.modules.forensic.domain import domain_intel
from mailforen.reports.generator import report_generator

# Configure
settings.debug = True
settings.rate_limit_delay = 2.0

# Create case
case_id = db.create_case("My Investigation", "target.com", "Description")

# Run checks
auth_result = auth_checker.check_all("target.com")
domain_result = domain_intel.get_all_records("target.com")

# Save findings
db.add_finding(case_id, "email.auth", "target.com", auth_result, "medium")
db.add_finding(case_id, "domain.intel", "target.com", domain_result, "info")

# Generate report
report_path = report_generator.generate(case_id, "html")
print(f"Report: {report_path}")

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Complete your first investigation in 5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• mailforen installed (Installation)
  • A suspicious .eml file (or use the example below)

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Case
docs.text:
mailforen case new "My-First-Investigation" \
  --target "example.com" \
  --desc "Learning mailforen workflow"

✓ Created case My-First-Investigation (ID: 1)

docs.title: Step 2: Analyze Email Headers
docs.text:
If you have a .eml file:

mailforen email headers suspicious.eml --case-id 1

Output includes: - From, To, Subject, Date, Message-ID - Received chain (hop-by-hop routing) - Authentication-Results - Originating IPs

docs.title: No .eml file? Create a test one:
docs.text:
cat > test.eml << 'EOF'
Return-Path: <attacker@phishersite.com>
Received: from mail.phishersite.com (unknown [203.0.113.100])
    by mx.victim.com (Postfix) with ESMTPS id ABC123
    for <user@victim.com>; Mon, 1 Jan 2024 10:00:00 +0000
Received: from [192.0.2.50] (helo=evil.local)
    by mail.phishersite.com with SMTP id XYZ789
    Mon, 1 Jan 2024 09:59:58 +0000
Authentication-Results: mx.victim.com; spf=fail smtp.mailfrom=phishersite.com
From: "IT Security" <security@company.com>
To: user@victim.com
Subject: URGENT: Password Reset Required
Date: Mon, 1 Jan 2024 10:00:01 +0000
Message-ID: <20240101100001.123@phishersite.com>
X-Mailer: EvilMailer 1.0

Click here to reset: https://bit.ly/fake-reset
EOF

mailforen email headers test.eml --case-id 1

docs.title: Step 3: Check Email Authentication
docs.text:
mailforen email auth phishersite.com --case-id 1

Output shows SPF, DMARC, and MX records. Risk level: - medium — SPF or DMARC missing - low — Both present

docs.title: Step 4: Investigate Infrastructure
docs.text:
# Domain DNS records
mailforen domain intel phishersite.com --case-id 1

# IP intelligence (from headers)
mailforen ip intel 203.0.113.100 --case-id 1

# Certificate transparency
mailforen ct search phishersite.com --case-id 1

docs.title: Step 5: Trace URLs
docs.text:
mailforen url trace "https://bit.ly/fake-reset" --case-id 1

Shows redirect chain (max 10 hops).

docs.title: Step 6: Generate Report
docs.text:
# HTML (view in browser)
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format html

# PDF (for evidence)
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format pdf

# JSON (for SIEM)
mailforen report generate --case-id 1 --format json

Reports saved to ~/.mailforen/reports/.

docs.title: Step 7: Review Case
docs.text:
mailforen case show 1

Shows case summary with all findings, risk levels color-coded.

docs.text:

  • Browse CLI Reference for all commands

docs.title: Authorized Use Only
docs.text:
mailforen is for authorized investigations only. You must have explicit, documented permission to investigate any target. Unauthorized use may violate:

  • Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (US)
  • Computer Misuse Act (UK)
  • GDPR (EU) — personal data processing
  • Local cybercrime laws

docs.title: Passive-First Design
docs.text:
Check Type Default Requires --unsafe DNS queries (SPF, DMARC, MX, A, etc.) ✅ Passive No Certificate Transparency (crt.sh) ✅ Passive No ipinfo.io ASN/geo lookup ✅ Passive No URL redirect tracing (HEAD/GET) ✅ Passive* No Username pivot (URL construction) ✅ Passive No File metadata (local) ✅ Passive No Future: SMTP VRFY/EXPN ❌ Active Yes Future: Direct target contact ❌ Active Yes

*URL tracing contacts the URL endpoint but follows standard HTTP semantics (no exploitation).

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
• Default: 1 request/second per HTTPClient instance
  • Configurable: MAILFOREN_RATE_LIMIT_DELAY
  • Applies to all HTTP calls (APIs, URL tracing)

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
• Default: 30 seconds
  • Configurable: MAILFOREN_TIMEOUT
  • Prevents hanging on slow/unresponsive targets

docs.title: Evidence Logging
docs.text:
• All findings timestamped and stored in SQLite
  • HTTP requests logged (when implemented)
  • Reports include generation timestamp and tool version

docs.title: No Credential Handling
docs.text:
• mailforen never stores or transmits credentials
  • API keys read from environment only
  • No authentication mechanisms implemented

docs.title: Unsafe Mode
docs.text:
mailforen --unsafe email auth example.com

⚠ Unsafe mode enabled: active checks may contact targets directly.

Currently: No active checks implemented. The flag exists as a gate for future features that may contact target systems directly (e.g., SMTP verification, web application scanning).

When active checks are added: They will call require_unsafe("action_name") which raises UnsafeModeRequired unless --unsafe was passed.

docs.title: What We Store Locally
docs.text:
• Case metadata (name, target, description)
  • Findings (module, input, results, risk level, tags, notes)
  • Logs (debug level to file, info to console)

docs.title: What We Don't Store
docs.text:
• No cloud sync
  • No telemetry
  • No automatic updates
  • No target data beyond what you explicitly analyze

docs.title: Data Retention
docs.text:
• You control ~/.mailforen/ — delete anytime
  • mailforen case delete — not yet implemented (manual SQLite)

docs.title: Reporting Security Issues
docs.text:
Found a vulnerability in mailforen itself?

  1. Do not open a public issue
  2. Email: security@[project-domain] (or GitHub Security Advisories)
  3. Include: description, reproduction steps, impact assessment

docs.title: Ethical Guidelines for Investigators
docs.text:
1. Scope — Define and document investigation scope before starting
  2. Minimize — Collect only data relevant to the investigation
  3. Document — Record all steps, tools, and timestamps
  4. Preserve — Maintain chain of custody for evidence
  5. Report — Share findings only with authorized stakeholders
  6. Destroy — Securely delete data when investigation concludes
